title: Lattice operator synopsis — night rotation
content:
Lattice operator synopsis — night rotation (compact)
Owner: Asha Patel
Shift: 2026-12-21 23:00 → 2026-12-22 07:00 UTC
Primary contact: asha@redwood.ai, pager: +1-555-0123 (sre-rotation)
Collaborators who jumped in: Miguel O., Evelyn Z.

Summary (TL;DR)
- Short window of elevated tail latency observed on embedding service (embed-proxy) between 00:18–00:35 UTC.
- Root cause likely a GPU-side memory fragmentation/leak on dedicated pool eu-west-1b; triggered longer GC on a small subset of hosts.
- Mitigation accepted: mark 3 hosts as draining, re-route traffic to warm spare pool; hotfix PR to kube-device-plugin rolled out (canary) at 01:12 UTC.
- No customer-visible error rates; elevated p50→p95 for embeddings only.

Chronological notes (raw)
- 00:16 — Observability alert: embed-proxy p95 > 550ms for 5m. Alert name: EMBED-P95-THRESH.
- 00:18 — I tail logs: a pattern of long CUDA allocations (OOM-like waits) on host eu-west-1b-gpu-07.
- 00:22 — Began draining eu-west-1b-gpu-07 via ASG + cordon; probe showed kernel messages pointing to nv-hostdriver warnings.
- 00:28 — Brief spike of internal retries added small additional latency; throttling bump prevented request errors.
- 00:32 — Spike subsided once traffic fully failed over to warm spares. p95 back to normal at 00:36.
- 01:08 — Deployed kube-device-plugin fix (PR 3124) to a canary host; metrics looked stable.
- 01:12 — Rolled canary to remainder of eu-west-1b; completed at 01:40.

Impact
- Customer-visible errors: none observed in SLO windows.
- Latency: embed-proxy p95 increased from 320ms baseline → 620ms (peak).
- Throughput: minimal reduction during host drain (~3% capacity dip for embeddings).

Immediate mitigations taken
- Drained affected hosts (eu-west-1b-gpu-07, -09, -11).
- Scaled up warm spare pool by +2 nodes temporarily (auto-scaler).
- Applied device-plugin patch (kube-device-plugin v1.8.1 -> v1.8.2-canary).
- Enabled additional logging on device-plugin + nv-hostdriver for 48h.

Follow-ups & action items (owners)
- SRE-789: Post-incident write-up and timeline (owner: Miguel Ortega) — due 2026-12-24.
- Runtime: add a memory-fragmentation metric export from our GPU driver shim (owner: Evelyn Zhang) — spike analysis will need granularity per-process. Target: 2027-01-05.
- Devinfra: update autoscaler policy to add a 3% buffer for embedding-heavy windows (owner: Priya Rao) — ticket created.
- Runbook delta: add an explicit section for "GPU host drain on nv-hostdriver warnings" with exact cordon/drain commands and telemetry thresholds (owner: Asha Patel) — quick patch by 2026-12-23.

Runbook notes & suggested edits (draft language)
- Current runbook step (drain-host): cordon node -> evict pods -> mark as reserve in inventory. Suggestion: insert a preflight check for device-plugin responsiveness and nv-hostdriver kernel logs (sudo dmesg | grep nv | tail -n 50).
- Add auto-scaling suggestion: when embedding queue depth > 120 and p95 > 450ms for 3 consecutive minutes, scale warm pool +2.
- Add diagnostic commands: "nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY" and "/opt/bin/gpu-metrics-exporter --sample 5s"

Noise / pager hygiene notes
- Several low-priority alerts flared during the incident (flapping k8s nodes with transient taints). We need to tune alert threshold to avoid signal fatigue — most were noise from repeated eviction drifts.\- Action: consolidate node-taint alert into a single aggregation window (owner: alerting-ops).

Outstanding questions (to resolve in write-up)
- Is the nv-hostdriver warning correlated with a recent kernel/driver bump on these hosts (check infra-rolling at 2026-12-18)?
- Why only a subset of hosts in eu-west-1b exhibited fragmentation? Hardware difference or workload skew?
- Should embedding routing prefer model-split across pools to reduce single-pool blast radius?

Quick checklist for incoming shift (what to watch first)
- Monitor EMBED-P95 & EMBED-QUEUE-DEPTH dashboards.
- Check device-plugin error counts (grafana -> cluster/device-plugin).
- Verify warm pool healthy count >= configured target (should be 5 for eu-west-1b).
- Verify kube-device-plugin version rollout status: rollout canary -> 100% -> monitor 15m before full roll if any errors.

Notes to follow during next 48h
- Keep debug logging on for device-plugin + nv-hostdriver for 48h (already enabled).
- Watch for eviction rate changes; if eviction_rate > 2/min on same hosts, consider full infra maintenance window.
- Miguel to attach kernel logs to SRE-789 and link GH PR for runtime tracing.

Hand-off specifics (my context for the next on-call)
- Where I left off: kube-device-plugin rolled out to eu-west-1b; 3 hosts still in reserve state pending infra checkbox. No ongoing errors, but elevated debug logs.
- Recommended immediate steps: confirm debug logs captured to S3 prefix s3://redwood-diagnostics/nv-hostdriver/2026-12-21-euwb; if absent, re-run log-capture script.

Misc notes / quick wins
- Small patch idea: add a jittered drain / randomized initial backoff so that when multiple hosts start evicting simultaneously, we avoid synchronous retries from embedding clients.
- Consider an embedding client-side backoff update to prefer cross-pool routing earlier in request lifecycle.

References & links
- Jira: SRE-789 (post-incident doc)
- GH PR: runtime#3124 (kube-device-plugin fix)
- Runbook proto: confluence://runbooks/gpu-memory-eviction

Signed-off: Asha Patel (on-call), 2026-12-22 07:55 UTC

-- end of compact operator synopsis --
